Theme

Time, the calendar & feasts

last adjective

the one before this

also last year, last time, previous, the night before, prior

classical

Cic. Har. Resp. 15: annō superiōre (Lewis & Short)
M-O s.v. last year: superiōre annō
Traupman 89: the previous year, superior annus
Traupman 43

superior, superius

adjective (comparative)

last, previous, earlier

annō superiōre, last year; superiōribus diēbus, in the previous days (Caes. BG 7.58, Lewis & Short); superiōre hebdomade, last week (see last week). Of nights, though, proximā nocte is last night and superiōre nocte the night before (Cic. Cat. 1.1).

Other words

  • proximus, proxima, proximum — last, most recent; or next

    adjective · also used · classical · Cic. Cat. 1.1: quid proximā, quid superiōre nocte ēgerīs; Traupman 87: last night, proximā nocte

    It means either the last or the next; the tense tells which (see last night, next week).

  • proximē — last time, most recently

    adverb · also used · classical · Caes. BG 3.29: cīvitātēs quae proximē bellum fēcerant (Lewis & Short); Plin. Ep. 4.13.3 (Lewis & Short)

  • prior, prius — earlier, former (of two)

    adjective, comparative · also used · classical · Liv. 3.9.7: priōre annō, the year before (Lewis & Short)

    The earlier of two, set against posterior; Cicero keeps superior for earlier in general, when no other time is named (Lewis & Short). Its neuter prius is the adverb before (see previously).

Examples

  • quid proximā, quid superiōre nocte ēgerīs

    what you did last night, and what the night beforeCic. Cat. 1.1

  • Annō superiōre in Lūsitāniā fuimus.

    Last year we were in Portugal.composed

See also last night, last week, next week, year, last, previously.
